text: 🇲🇽✊ "How is it possible that a loan does not go down as you keep paying it?" "Because they built it to always take money from the worker." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas On Dec 31 last year, 4,856,000 "unpayable" Infonavit loans were restructured — debts that grew no matter how much workers paid. Today there is no requirement to get a home, and 75% of recipients are young people.

🇲🇽✊ 1.8 million homes. Close to 30 million people. "We are building 1 million 800 thousand homes... we are going to help close to 30 million people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas The program is already adding close to 1% of GDP to Mexico's economic growth. In Chiapas the goal is 70,000 new homes this term — over 23,000 already delivered.

🇲🇽✊ "We call ourselves humanists for one simple reason: we govern for the people." "For 36 years of neoliberalism, Infonavit stopped building homes — it handed out loans designed to keep taking the worker's money. We changed that." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas In housing it is easy to tell the difference between neoliberal governments and humanist ones. Mexico is building homes again — not debt.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>HOMICIDES DOWN 49% — MEXICO PROVES YOU DON'T NEED MASS INCARCERATION</u>

Homicides in Mexico are down 49% under Sheinbaum — from 86.9 a day in September 2024 to 44.3.

No mano dura, no mass incarceration: 2,400 meth labs dismantled, fentanyl trafficking at the border cut sharply, and thousands of young people pulled into school and work instead of cartels. Attack the causes, not just the symptoms.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SOFT COUP IN THE GROUP STAGE — FOREIGN OPERATIVES RUN A DISINFO WAR ON MEXICO</u>

While Mexico hosts the World Cup, a foreign-run disinformation machine is working to brand it a "failed state." Contralínea names the operatives: Argentina's Fernando Cerimedo (probed by Brazil for electoral disinfo) and Spain's Javier Negre (convicted for fabricating news), pushing a soft-coup line alongside the US Embassy and the PAN.

Mexico's legal counsel laid it out publicly — right of reply, on the record.

🇲🇽🌊 <u>THE BAY IS NOT FOR SALE — MAYO-YOREME BLOCK A $1.6B AMMONIA PLANT</u>

The Mayo-Yoreme of Sinaloa are still blocking GPO's $1.6 billion ammonia plant on Ohuira Bay — a 2,220-ton-a-day facility they say threatens the mangroves, the fishing, and the people with a toxic gas leak.

Children walked the Topolobampo shoreline chanting "¡Aquí no!" Twelve years of permits, and the bay still isn't for sale.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>TENOCHTITLAN REOPENS — MEXICO WALKS BACK INTO THE TEMPLE THE EMPIRE BURIED</u>

For the first time, Mexico opens the Temple of Ehécatl and the ballcourt of Tenochtitlan to the public — sacred Mexica structures buried under the colonial capital, walkable through July 19 as part of the "Mundial Social."

INAH calls the ballcourt Teotlachco, "the game of the gods." The empire poured a cathedral on top of it; the city dug it back out.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>MORENA MOVES TO ABOLISH 'SUBSTITUTE' LEGISLATORS — IF A SEAT EMPTIES, VOTERS DECIDE</u>

Morena's Alfonso Ramírez Cuéllar is pushing a structural reform to scrap the figure of the legislative "suplente" — the unelected stand-in who inherits a deputy's or senator's seat the moment the titleholder steps aside. Under his proposal, a vacated seat would trigger a fresh election instead of an automatic handoff. "Substitutes are unnecessary," he said. "Citizens should always choose who represents them in the Chamber."
